feature: Predict, test and revise captured sea-route crossing forecasts
changes: A folded chance investigation extends each recorded directed route. Students choose birds or plants, an inclusive count range and a reason, then test their forecast against 16 fresh possible dispersal rounds.
Each prediction and reason is locked before its new non-overlapping block of private draws; up to eight forecasts and 128 possible rounds are retained for this view.

The exact count distribution reuses the existing probability-convolution helper. Probability bars, private sample frequencies, recorded-arrival marker, zero-crossing chance and range probability distinguish theory from observations.
Private dispatches use one draw per source individual to choose the first outbound route, second outbound route or staying. Every possible round restarts the same captured source cohort.
Students review earlier frozen forecasts, compare hits with expected coverage, inspect conserved dispatch counts and revise the next range without rewriting earlier evidence.

Tiny positive probabilities display below 0.01%, and nearly certain ranges above 99.99%, preserving the distinction from impossibility and certainty, including a positive excluded tail whose sum rounds to one.
Bounded route/round/species drafts, separate Learning Journal entries and complete source-checkpoint/forecast-recipe exports rebuild results rather than trusting saved outcome values.
The lab is lazy, responsive and keyboard accessible. No breeding, mutation, newcomer inheritance or new founding population is generated by practice dispatches.

coverage: Ten new checks compare exact PMFs and moments with an independent binomial formula, including N6 versus N24, closed routes and empty cohorts.
Private seed and dispatch reconstruction, three mutually exclusive destinations, unique fresh seeds, inclusive ranges and the full eight-block 128-draw partition.
G0 and invalid context/bounds rejection; captured settings and previous source remain independent of queued settings, current expedition RNG, later generations and actual recorded newborn outcomes.
Recorded world, next RNG future, actual newborns and inherited copies remain unchanged.
Existing route evidence, partner selection, two-species engine, repeated research, generation story, gene flow, connection timeline, caseboard and science checks.

renderGoldens.scope: Only the two EvoLab digest entries changed for new CSS; default structure remains 49 buttons, six inputs and one SVG.

coverage: Two new desktop/phone journeys verify exact PMFs independently, displayed chart probabilities and sampled frequencies, frozen ranges/reasons, fresh 16-draw blocks and the 128-draw limit.
Full source-checkpoint replay reconstructs every private trial and forecast result; sample counts conserve the preceding source population.
Rare positive outcomes and nearly certain ranges have truthful bounded labels; exact probability table agrees with the chart.

Private practice preserves actual arrival, reproducing-parent and inherited-copy evidence; separate journal entries, queued-setting protection, archived generations, scoped route/species drafts and remount restoration.
Keyboard range limits and coupled endpoints, native selectors, 44px buttons, reduced-motion/no-WebGL phone, zero axe WCAG 2 A/AA and 2.1 AA violations and no horizontal page overflow.
Nine existing archipelago, partner microscope, route evidence and private repeated-study journeys passed with a real drawn desktop WebGL scene.
browser.initialIssuesResolved: Focused phone checks exposed dynamic range labels and wrapped select option text in accessible names. Stable accessible names were added to the new lab’s ranges, selectors and reason field; the complete final suite passed.

visualReview: Final desktop and phone screenshots inspected: clear forecast controls, readable probability/sample chart, frozen forecast review, conserved dispatch counts, responsive cards and native selectors.

scientificBoundaries: The selected-route marginal is binomial: fixed previous-cohort N, the same selected-route probability for every source individual, and independent modeled dispatch decisions. Other-route movement and staying both belong to the complement of the selected route.
The sampler retains the full three-destination categorical decision rather than drawing the two sea routes independently. One individual can take at most one route per practice round.

Possible rounds are conditional repeated dispersal samples from the same captured source and settings. They do not chain generations, resample founders, alter weather, change queued controls, or consume the expedition RNG.

The exact model range probability is outcome coverage, not a confidence interval, p-value or guarantee. A small empirical frequency need not equal that probability or approach it monotonically as draws are added.

The observed expedition count remains fixed and separate from hypothetical draws. Practice creates no births, trait mutations or marker-copy contributions; recorded families and newborn inheritance remain actual historical evidence.
Forecast ranges and reasons are captured before each next non-overlapping block of 16 draws. Later revisions do not rewrite earlier forecasts.

Probabilities are evaluated numerically. Positive tiny values retain a positive-bound label, and a broad range excluding a positive tail does not display certainty solely because its accumulated probability rounds to one.
An empty source or zero dispersal gives a degenerate zero-crossing distribution. G0 has no captured round and exposes no invented chance investigation.
Distances, species and dispersal coefficients remain fictional teaching assumptions. This is not empirical validation of Galapagos ecology or a causal coevolution test.
